name: Sacred Sha, Mythic
body:
MYTHIC SACRED SHA
CR 7/MR 3

XP 3,200
LE Medium magical beast (mythic)
Init +6; Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision, sandstorm sight; Perception +9

DEFENSE

AC 25, touch 17, flat-footed 18 (+6 Dex, +1 dodge, +8 natural)
hp 93 (6d10+60)
Fort +10, Ref +11, Will +6
DR 5/epic and good; Resist cold 10, fire 10; SR 14

OFFENSE

Speed 40 ft.
Melee bite +12 (2d6+8 plus 1d6 electricity, disease, and trip)
Special Attacks disease, mythic power (3/day, surge ++1d6), sandstorm, smite good (1/day, +2 attack, +6 damage), smite unbeliever

STATISTICS

Str 22, Dex 23, Con 20, Int 9, Wis 19, Cha 14
Base Atk +6; CMB +12; CMD 28 (32 vs. trip)
Feats Combat Reflexes, Dodge, Following Step, Step Upmf
Skills Acrobatics +10, Perception +9, Stealth +12
Languages Common, Infernal

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Befuddling Gaze (Su)

As a standard action, a mythic sacred sha can look at an opponent within 90 feet and drive it temporarily insane, rendering it confused for 1d6 rounds (DC 15 Will negates). The save DC is Charisma-based and includes the mythic sha’s mythic rank as a racial bonus. By expending one use of mythic power as a swift action, the sha can instead affect all targets in a 45-foot cone.

Disease (Su)

Shas transmit potent disease with their bites. The most common form of disease carried by a sha drives its victims insane, reducing them to babbling fools or raving lunatics.

Touch of Madness: Bite-injury; save Fort DC 21; onset 1d3 days; frequency 1/day; effect 1d4 Wis damage and 1d4 Cha damage; cure 2 consecutive saves.

A mythic sacred sha adds its mythic rank to the disease‘s save DC. By expending one use of mythic power as an immediate action, it causes the diseased creature to become contagious. The victim inflicts the disease on any creature it touches or that touches it with natural weapons or unarmed strikes. The Fort save DC is reduced to 17 for disease inflicted by the affected creature. The mythic sha is immune to this disease.

Sandstorm (Ex)

Once per day as a full-round action, a sha can create a sandstorm. The sandstorm has a radius of 100 feet centered on the sha and lasts for 1 minute per Hit Die the sha possesses (6 minutes for a typical sha).

For the first minute of mythic sacred sha’s sandstorm, it deals 1d8 points of electricity damage (Fort DC 18 half) to each creature caught in the sandstorm. It can extend this period by an additional minute by expending one use of mythic power as a swift action.

Sandstorm Sight (Su)

A sha can see clearly in a naturally occurring sandstorm or one created by it or another sha using its sandstorm ability.

Smite Unbeliever (Su)

Once per day, a mythic sacred sha may smite a creature that does not worship its patron(s), as per its smite good ability. Against a divine spellcaster that does not worship its patron(s), the sha doubles its damage. The smite lasts until the target is dead or until the sha rests. It can expend one use of mythic power as a swift action to use this ability again.

ECOLOGY

Environment warm deserts
Organization solitary, pair, or pack (1 mythic sacred sha plus 1-4 sacred shas and 3-8 shas)
Treasure none

The strangely shaped glowing red eyes, unnaturally upright ears, and split tail betray the unnatural origins of this black canine. Shas possess a distinctly canine appearance and are often mistaken at night for common jackals whose eyes are illuminated by firelight. Black fur, tinted with the dust and sand of the desert, covers a sha’s body. The creature’s spiralended eyes glow a dull red. Explorers report that seeing a sha’s eyes glowing in the dark night is often the only indication of an impending attack. A sha’s strong jaw, lined with razor-sharp teeth, allows the creature to drag down larger prey in a fashion similar to that of a wolf. Standing at chest height to most humans, shas weigh between 100 and 150 pounds.

Villagers whisper that a sha nears when they spot faint red lights in the distance, believing those lights to be the creatures’ menacing eyes. Many times, these sightings are only imagined, but shas do prowl near settlements and keep an eye on humankind. Shas’ urge to hunt people who have ceased to remember and honor their patrons drives them to attack caravans, harass remote villages, and prowl isolated oases to slaughter humanoids.

When alone, a sha spends its days trekking the vast wastelands of the desert, prowling among lost monuments of ancient times. While wandering the deserts, shas attack small convoys or groups of nomads along the desert fringes.

Using their innate ability to conjure sandstorms, shas close in on the unsuspecting groups and try to bite as many different enemies as possible, then retreat before their foes can regroup. By doing this, the shas ensure that survivors return to civilization mad with disease and then spread the sickness to others or act on their insane urges.

When packs of shas come together, they usually do so because a number of their kind happen upon each other in pursuit of a caravan or some other nomadic prey, then decide to continue hunting together once they feed. Packs quickly dissolve as prey grows scarce.
